newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine alumina plant does not want new investors.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine alumina plant does not want new investors.

text.p: The head of Ukraine's sole alumina plant is pushing local authorities to give a controlling stake to employees, which would stop foreign investors from buying shares in the company, a regional official said on Tuesday.

The Mykolayiv regional government has asked the State Property Fund to give workers at Mykolayivsky Hlynozemny Zavod (MHZ) the right to acquire an extra 25 percent shares, Volodymyr Dubov, head of the domestic economic department, told Reuters.

The move would effectively prevent a foreign investor from buying shares in MHZ and give control to the workers, already awarded the right to buy 30.97 percent shares by a government commission last month.

Dubov said by telephone from the Black Sea port of Mykolayiv that the regional government had approved the request to increase workers' shares after an appeal from MHZ chief executive Vitaly Meshyn, who is opposed to foreign investment.
Ukrainian news agency Ukrinform reported Meshyn as saying that giving workers an extra 25 percent shares could prevent foreign companies from taking over the plant.
"Foreign companies, including those who control alumina plants in Russia, have not given up their intentions to run NHZ," Meshyn was quoted as saying.

MHZ, which receives most of its bauxite from West Africa and sends 90 percent of its output to Russian aluminium smelters, is one of 208 state enterprises that Ukraine plans to put out for strategic investment tender.
MHZ, which has authorised capital of $178 million, is the dominant raw materials supplier for Russia's -- and the world's -- two biggest aluminium smelters.
The country's highest court in August denied the workers' collective the right to own a 40.14 percent stake in the plant.
Under a plan which MHZ has agreed with the State Property Fund, 25.1 percent of shares would remain in government hands.
About 25 percent would go to a strategic investor and about six percent would be auctioned for privatisation certificates.

The company has forecast 1996 output at 1.0 million tonnes, and produced 996,000 tonnes of alumina in 1995. Whatever is not exported to Russia goes to Ukraine's only smelter at Zaporizhya. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
